subject: health
title: Healthy Teeth
about: Brushing for two minutes morning and bedtime with a pea of toothpaste, spitting it out, flossing, brushing the tongue, dentist checkups, wiggly teeth, cavities and sugar, tooth-friendly snacks and water, and a mouthguard for sports. NC 1.PCH.1.3 (baby teeth give way to permanent teeth; dental care); builds on Healthy Habits for Dental Health Month in February.
tip: Set a two-minute timer or play one song tonight and brush along with him.

cards.q: How long do you brush your teeth each time?
cards.note: Play one song. Brush until it ends.

cards.q: When do you brush your teeth?
cards.note: Two times a day, two minutes each time.

cards.q: How much toothpaste goes on your brush?
cards.note: A dot the size of a pea is plenty for kids. A grown-up can squeeze it.

cards.q: After you brush, do you swallow the toothpaste or spit it out?
cards.note: Spit, then rinse your brush. Toothpaste is for teeth, not tummies.

cards.q: What cleans between your teeth where a brush cannot reach?
cards.note: Floss once a day. A grown-up can help until your hands get the hang of it.

cards.q: Which part of your mouth should you brush too, for fresh breath?
cards.note: Germs sit on your tongue. A gentle brush sweeps them off.

cards.q: How often do you visit the dentist for a checkup?
cards.note: Many kids go every six months. The dentist counts, cleans and checks your teeth.

cards.q: What does the dentist use to see the backs of your teeth?
cards.note: The little mirror on a stick lets the dentist see every side.

cards.q: Your tooth is wiggly. What do you do?
cards.note: Tell a grown-up. It will come out on its own when it is ready.

cards.q: Baby teeth fall out and grown-up teeth grow in. How many grown-up teeth will you have?
cards.note: Most grown-ups have 32 teeth, counting the four wisdom teeth that come last.
Germs in your mouth turn sugar into acid that makes little holes. Brushing stops them.

cards.q: What do the germs on your teeth love to eat?
cards.note: That is why sticky, sweet treats are sometimes foods.

cards.q: Which snack is good for your teeth?
cards.note: Cheese, apples, carrots and milk all help teeth. Crunchy veggies scrub them too.

cards.q: Which drink is best for your teeth?
cards.note: Water washes away sugar and has no sugar of its own.

cards.q: You ate a sweet treat. What helps your teeth right after?
cards.note: Swish some water around, then brush at bedtime.

cards.q: What protects your teeth when you play sports?
cards.note: A mouthguard is a soft shield you wear over your teeth.

cards.q: How often do you get a new toothbrush?
cards.note: Sooner if the bristles look bent and frayed.
A toothbrush carries your germs. Everyone gets their own.
